scope: Read-only source comparison and authored development examples; not a production accuracy benchmark. No provider keys read or external requests made.
caveats: These examples were used during development, so percentages would not estimate real-world accuracy.
Offline comparisons do not compare the default AI-enabled prototype against an AI-disabled current app as an accuracy contest.
The benign-AI experiment uses the same mocked valid answer only to isolate result merging, not to measure model accuracy.
OCR, image pixels, live website reputation and model providers are not accuracy-benchmarked in this report.

sourceFindings.prototype: AI enabled automatically when configured; unclear/suspicious checks use meaning review.
sourceFindings.current: AI help starts off and must be selected; enabling it reviews all supported text/URL/OCR/QR submissions.

sourceFindings.finding: Final display uses the completed detector verdict and its retained evidence. The browser runs shared contextual rules when disconnected.
The original SMS model weights are identical
sourceFindings.detail: The old 97.44% archived score measures a spam/ham classifier, not scam accuracy or the full application. The prototype documentation says its newer detection changes were not accuracy-evaluated.

sourceFindings.finding: Current OCR retries difficult reads and exposes extraction uncertainty and editable text.
Current image-origin mode checks file provenance offline, then separately reviews pixels when online sharing is selected.
Current version also adds useful detection layers
sourceFindings.detail: Current backend includes exact reference matches, advisory dataset models, improved protective-advice handling, and cash-in/winnings context rules. These should be evaluated separately from frontend integration faults.
